CITY OF LA VERNE
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  Wednesday, March 9, 2022

1.  Chairperson Simison called the regular meeting of the La Verne Planning
  Commission to order at 6:30 p.m.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Commissioner Simison led the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL: Planning Commissioners present: Thomas Allison, Jeffry
  Allred, Jeremy Conrad, and Jason Simison. Planning Commissioner not
  present: Jason Lorge. Advisory personnel present: Community
  Development Director Eric Scherer, City Attorney Bob Kress, Principal
  Planner Candice Bowcock and Secretary Natalie Hiatt.

4.  PUBLIC COMMENT

  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

5.  CONTINUED CASE NO. 07-22GPA; HOUSING ELEMENT UPDATE

  Ms. Bowcock stated that the Draft 2021-2029 Housing Element Update
  was submitted in December 2021, to the California Department of Housing
  and Community Development. A comment letter was received from HCD
  on February 1, 2022 requesting that some areas of the draft be enhanced.
  Staff submitted to the HCD again on February 18, 2022, a response will
  be received after the 60 day review period. Staff is recommending that the
  Planning Commission continue the meeting to a date to be determined.

  It was moved Commissioner Conrad and seconded by Commissioner
  Allison to continue the Public Hearing to a date to be determined. Motion
  carried by a 4-0 vote.

6.  CASE NO. 103-21VAR; VARIANCE TO ENCROACH INTO THE
  REQUIRED SIDE AND REAR SETBACKS FOR AN ACCESSORY
  STRUCTURE AT THE HOME LOCATED AT 5075 OLD RANCH ROAD

  Ms. Bowcock presented her staff report.
 Planning Commission Minutes
March 9, 2022
  Commissioner Simison opened the public hearing.

  The applicants Ryan and Kellie Racine were present at the meeting. Mr.
  Racine stated 2 out of the 4 setbacks are in violation within inches. The
  property is unique and due to the flag shaped lot, it does not disturb the
  adjacent neighbors. He stated that it was not their intent to create the
  space as it is now.

  There were four neighbors that spoke in support of the variance.

  Mrs. Racine stated that the pandemic created a need for more space and
  privacy as they were working from home.

  Chairperson Simison closed the public hearing.

  The Commissioners asked staff why the DRC denied the request for a
  variance.

  Ms. Bowcock stated concerns that the bathroom construction was
  purposely done to break the code.

  Commissioner Conrad asked the Racine’s if the plumbing was put in prior
  to foundation. He stated that he wants to support City staff and not set a
  precedent.

  Chairperson Simison re-opened the public hearing.

  Mrs. Racine stated that their contractor and friend guided them into putting
  plumbing in place in case it was converted at a later time. She stated they
  would not have installed and removed the windows if they were going to
  change the structure.

  Chairperson Simison closed the public hearing.

  It was moved by Commissioner Conrad and seconded by Commissioner
  Allison to approve option #2, approving the setback variance request,
  changing the permitted patio to an accessory structure, allowing the
  bathroom to remain, but requiring the applicant to obtain all necessary
  permits for all of the illegal work that was done that was not a part of the
  original approved plans, paying double the permit fees. Motion was carried
  by a 4-0 vote.

OTHER MATTERS/INFORMATION

7.  FOOTHILL GOLD LINE UPDATE

  2
 Planning Commission Minutes
March 9, 2022
  Lisa Levy Buch, Chief Communications and strategic Development Officer
  of Foothill Gold Line, presented a project update for the Planning
  Commission.

  The Commissioners asked questions regarding security, timeline of the
  construction, and parking.

8.  DEVELOPMENT UPDATE

  Ms. Bowock presented an update which included a list of new businesses
  and upcoming development projects.

  Mr. Scherer discussed the pedestrian bridge from the Gold Line platform
  to the Fairplex. He announced that the President approved an earmark of
  $4,000,000 in funds for the project.

ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 7:57 p.m. The next regular meeting of the
  Planning Commission will be held April 13, 2022 at 6:30 p.m. in the
  Council Chambers, 3660 “D” Street, La Verne, CA 91750.
